name: POLAND

flag.title: Biało-Czerwona
flag.note: White over red — simple, bold, unmistakable

lead: Poland sits in the middle of Europe on a big flat plain. Its capital was rebuilt from rubble. A white eagle has been its symbol for over a thousand years. Nearly 38 million people live here.

sections.wows: 7 things to make you go wow

geo: Poland is mostly one big flat plain. Armies could march across it. The Vistula and Oder rivers flow north to the Baltic Sea.
The Tatra Mountains rise along the Slovak border in the south. Ibex (wild goats) leap between rocky cliffs. The ancient Białowieża Forest spreads through the east.
animals: The European bison is Europe's heaviest land animal. By 1927, none were left in the wild. Scientists bred them from zoo animals. Over 2,000 now roam free. The biggest herd lives in Białowieża Forest.
Brown bears, wolves, and lynx live in the Tatra Mountains. The lynx, a wild cat, has huge paws for walking on snow. White storks nest on village chimneys.
culture: Pierogi are dough pockets stuffed with potato, cheese, or berries. Żurek is sour rye soup. Bigos is hunter's stew. Amber from the Baltic coast has been traded for 3,000 years.
The composer Frédéric Chopin was Polish. Every five years, pianists compete in Warsaw's Chopin Competition. At Christmas, families leave an extra plate for a stranger in need.
history: Poland became a kingdom over 1,000 years ago. By the 16th century, it was one of Europe's biggest states. Then three neighbours split it up. Poland vanished from maps for 123 years.
Poland returned in 1918. In World War II, Warsaw was nearly destroyed, and six million citizens were killed. In 1989, the Solidarity union won Poland's first free elections peacefully.
wows: Poland vanished from world maps for 123 years, yet its language survived.
Warsaw's Old Town was rebuilt using 18th-century paintings.
Marie Curie, born in Warsaw in 1867, won Nobel Prizes in two sciences.
Poland crafts about 70% of the world's amber jewellery.
Bison vanished from the wild by 1927, yet 2,000+ roam now.
About 25% of the world's white storks nest in Poland.
Wieliczka Salt Mine has chapels and chandeliers made of salt.

myths.myth: Poland is always cold and grey
myths.fact: Summers often hit 30°C. Kraków and Gdańsk are sunny, colourful cities.

myths.myth: Polish spelling is impossible to learn
myths.fact: Each letter makes one sound. Learn that sz is sh and cz is ch, and it gets easy.
